work.permit: Leyfi Vinnueftirlits ríkisins (Administration of Occupational Safety and Health)

note: Majority: 18, the legal age law (lögræðislög nr. 71/1997) as island.is, the government's portal, states it: one becomes lögráða, both sjálfráða and fjárráða, at 18. The law itself on althingi.is answers this client with a Cloudflare 'Just a moment' page, and an archive.org snapshot (2026-08-31) was asked for twelve times and reset each time. Emancipation by marriage isn't held. Work: 15. Regulation nr. 426/1999 on the work of young people (island.is): a barn is under 15 or in compulsory schooling, and children may not be hired unless the regulation says otherwise (art. 24), so the age is 15 once compulsory school is done; light work from 13 (art. 25) and municipal work schools (art. 26) aren't held. Performers: art. 34 lets children, including those under 13, be hired for cultural, artistic, sports and advertising events; for a child under 13 a permit (leyfi) of Vinnueftirlit ríkisins is needed before hiring, while those over 13 need none except to depart from the hours rules: the 13-and-over freedom isn't held. Service: none. Iceland has no armed forces: the Ministry for Foreign Affairs (15 September 2025) says that, as a state without armed forces, Iceland relies on cooperation with allies.

sources.title: Ísland.is: Lögræði, sjálfræði og fjárræði
sources.said: Einstaklingar verða lögráða við 18 ára aldur, bæði sjálfráða og fjárráða.

sources.title: Ísland.is: Reglugerð nr. 426/1999 um vinnu barna og unglinga
sources.said: Barn merkir í reglugerð þessari einstakling undir 15 ára aldri eða sem er í skyldunámi. ... Börn má ekki ráða í vinnu nema annað sé sérstaklega tekið fram ... Afla skal leyfis frá Vinnueftirliti ríkisins áður en til ráðningar kemur vegna vinnu barna yngri en 13 ára. ... Börn eldri en 13 ára er heimilt að ráða til að taka þátt í starfsemi skv. 1. mgr. án sérstaks leyfis.

sources.title: Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Iceland (15 September 2025): Report by panel of parliamentarians outlines key elements of a defence and security policy
sources.said: As a state without armed forces, Iceland relies on cooperation with allies for deterrence and defence
